subject: Re: Replacement cost visibility and billing-cycle alignment for Verdant Labs
messages:
From: Maria Gomez <maria.gomez@verdant-labs.com>
To: connor_obrien <connor_obrien@redwood.ai>
Cc: Paul Rivers <paul.rivers@verdant-labs.com>
Date: Tue, 1 Dec 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Replacement cost visibility and billing-cycle alignment

Hi Connor,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the throughput numbers were really helpful. We're starting an internal review to compare switching some inference workload off our incumbent provider and onto Redwood. Two operational things are tripping us up: a) we need a line-by-line replacement cost view (instance/GPU-hours, token unit price, egress, support) that maps to our existing invoice, and b) our finance team wants to align billing cycles (we run on calendar quarter prepay; their procurement prefers month-to-month for pilot months).

Can you send a concise replacement cost sheet and call out any packaging/seat/commit tradeoffs? Also, what flexibility do you have on short-term pilots that live on a different billing cadence than annual reserved capacity?

Goal is to present to the procurement team on Friday (12/4).

Appreciate it —
Maria

Maria Gomez
VP Engineering, Platform
Verdant Labs

Maria — thanks for the clear ask and the Friday deadline. Looping in Grace (finance) and Stephanie (product ops) so we can get you: 1) a single-sheet replacement view that maps Redwood line items to your current invoice categories, and 2) a few billing/packaging options with pros/cons for pilot vs committed capacity.

Quick clarifications so we target the sheet correctly:
- Do you want token-level breakouts by model family (LlamaX / Red-3 / Red-3-8bit) or a blended token rate?
- Are there any required add-ons (SLA, additional log retention, private VPC) we should assume?

We should be able to get a first-pass spreadsheet to you later today and a final version tomorrow.

Connor O'Brien
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
From: grace_oconnor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>

Cc: stephanie_nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 1 Dec 2026 15:48:00 -0800
Subject: RE: Replacement cost visibility and billing-cycle alignment

Hi Maria / Connor — attached is Verdant_cost_model_v3.xlsx and a short explainer (billing-cycle-options.pdf). Highlights (summary section on first tab):

- Scenario A (Pilot, month-to-month): small pilot pool (1-2 GPUs equivalent), blended token rate with 10% pilot discount, no long-term commit. Ideal for testing integration; higher unit price but no billing reschedule required.
- Scenario B (Quarterly prepay): three-month prepay with 15% blended discount and 30% on egress. Matches your current quarterly cadence; discounts apply to reserved compute only.
- Scenario C (Reserved annual): annual commit with tiered pricing by token volume; lowest per-token cost, includes 24/7 premium support and 90-day price protection.

Line items included: GPU compute (GPU-hr), model license/pack (when applicable), per-token inference fee, egress, support/observability retention surcharge, optional private deployment fee. Each line maps to the comparable description on your current invoice (invoice sample column).

Edge notes:
- We can prorate a pilot that runs into a quarterly prepay: credits for pilot months can be applied against the first quarter of a prepay if you choose Scenario B mid-quarter.
- For private VPC deployments, there is a one-time onboarding fee (listed) and a separate networking egress profile.

Attachments: Verdant_cost_model_v3.xlsx (spreadsheet) — contains model families split and blended views; billing-cycle-options.pdf — short decision table for procurement.

Grace O'Connor
Finance, Commercial Operations | Redwood Inference
From: Maria Gomez <maria.gomez@verdant-labs.com>
To: connor_obrien <connor_obrien@redwood.ai>
Cc: Paul Rivers <paul.rivers@verdant-labs.com>, grace_oconnor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 2 Dec 2026 08:22:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Replacement cost visibility and billing-cycle alignment

Grace — thanks, that spreadsheet is exactly the format procurement wanted. A couple of follow-ups from Paul (cc'd):

1) On the pilot discount: can you extend the pilot price to include 500K tokens per month at the pilot rate for the first two months (we expect variable usage)?
2) Billing alignment: if we start a pilot mid-quarter and then convert to Quarterly prepay (Scenario B), can you confirm the calendar for when credits apply and whether that affects uplift pricing?
3) Packaging: we currently have a blended model mix (40% small gen, 60% embeddings). Can you confirm the blended token rate would remain within +/- 3% of the representative blended line in the spreadsheet if we change model mix by +/- 10%?

We will share the sheet internally on Friday; if we can get these three answers today that would be ideal.

Thanks —
Maria
From: connor_obrien <connor_obrien@redwood.ai>
To: Maria Gomez <maria.gomez@verdant-labs.com>
Cc: grace_oconnor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>, stephanie_nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 3 Dec 2026 14:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Replacement cost visibility and billing-cycle alignment

Maria / Paul — quick answers below and proposed next steps:  

1) Pilot token extension: Yes, we can guarantee 500K tokens/month at the pilot rate for the first two months. We'll capture this as a time-boxed credit line in the SOW (no change to the pilot monthly invoice, credit applied afterward unless you elect immediate netting).

2) Mid-quarter conversion: Credits from the pilot can be applied to the first invoice of the quarterly prepay period; if conversion happens mid-quarter, the credit will be prorated to the quarter in which the conversion occurs. No retroactive uplift to the per-token price — the prepay discount applies from the first day of the prepay term.

3) Blended rate sensitivity: The blended token rate in the sheet assumes your stated mix; small shifts (±10%) change blended rate by ~1.2–2.8% depending on model family mix. We included a sensitivity tab in the spreadsheet; happy to run a quick reblend after you provide a 30-day usage sample.

Proposed next steps:
- We'll update the spreadsheet to add the explicit 500K/month pilot credit line and a one-slide summary you can hand to procurement; you should have that by EOD today.
- If procurement wants, we can schedule a 30-minute call Thursday to walk through the credit mechanics and the sample invoice mapping.

Would you like Thursday 10:00am PT?

Connor O'Brien
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Attachments referenced: Verdant_cost_model_v3.xlsx, billing-cycle-options.pdf
